observations: A large skull-like form fills the frame in profile, built from overlapping loops of pink, yellow, cyan, and red lines against a solid black ground.
A jagged yellow crown shape sits at the upper right, its five pointed peaks drawn in a continuous stroke, resting near the top of the head.
Two spiral-centered eye forms appear at different depths—one purple with a white spiral core at center-left, one cyan loop to the right—while yellow horizontal bars suggest bared teeth at the bottom.
reading: Layered neon outlines trace and retrace a skull seen from the side, each color pass slightly offset so the form appears to vibrate against the black field. The crown reads less as decoration than as another restless loop, no more stable than the skull beneath it. A grinning unease comes through the bared-teeth bars and the mismatched, staring eye spirals, which refuse to settle into a single expression.
contextAngle: As the highest title number and last recorded creation in the owned Scrimshaw subset, this work sits at the current boundary of the collection. Its title neighbor Scrimshaw 41 shares the skull-and-teeth motif but uses denser black hatching rather than bright separated color loops.

connections.reason: Both show skull forms with spiral eyes and exposed teeth, but Scrimshaw 41 buries its structure under heavy black cross-hatching while this work isolates each color line against open black space.
Both pack a round head shape with competing neon colors and bared-teeth bars, though rawblocks #40 fills the background with pink and cyan blobs while Scrimshaw 42 keeps its black ground empty.

lookingQuestion: Where the colored outlines overlap and diverge around the jaw, do they read as one skull shifting position or as several separate heads stacked together?
ambiguities: Whether the profile faces strictly left or is a three-quarter view is unclear—the second eye and ear-like loop on the right could indicate a second facing direction.
Small colored marks inside the cranium area may be additional features or residual line crossings; their role is hard to resolve at this scale.
